intro: Dartington is a village beside the River Dart, just north of Totnes in south Devon, best known for Dartington Hall and its grounds. West of the hall stands the tower of the old parish church, pulled down in 1873, and around it grow ancient yews, the biggest measured since 1787. A reader recorded one of them for us beside the tower.
meta_description: The ancient yews round the old church tower at Dartington Hall in Devon, measured since 1787: what is known about them and how to find them.
question_meta: The oldest trees at Dartington are the ancient yews round the old church tower by Dartington Hall, measured since 1787.
question_answer: The ancient yews in the old churchyard round the tower of the former St Mary's church, just west of Dartington Hall. The biggest, a female yew west of the tower, measured 655 centimetres round in 2012.
question_context: Dartington's parish church stood beside Dartington Hall until 1873, when it was pulled down and only its tower was kept. The yews that grew round it are still there. The Ancient Yew Group, which records old yews across Britain, lists three. The biggest is a female tree on the west side of the tower, first mentioned in 1787 when Richard Polwhele measured it. In 1962 Alan Mitchell recorded 716 centimetres at five feet, in 1999 the group's recorder found 658 close to the ground, and in 2012 it was 655 at fifteen centimetres; its trunk is knobbly, with nails still embedded in it. A fluted yew south-west of the tower measured 434 centimetres in 2008, and a sprawling yew on a bank to the north has not been measured. The group puts the churchyard in its ancient band. A reader sent us one of these yews beside the tower, with a girth of about eight metres by their own measure. The grounds of Dartington Hall are open to visitors.

faq.q: How old are the Dartington yews?
faq.a: Nobody has dated them. The Ancient Yew Group lists the biggest as ancient, and it has been measured since 1787.

faq.q: Where are the yews at Dartington Hall?
faq.a: Round the tower of the former St Mary's church, the lone tower just west of Dartington Hall. The biggest stands on the west side of the tower.
Yes. The old churchyard is in the grounds of Dartington Hall, which are open to visitors; check the estate's hours before you go.

trees.story:
The church at Dartington was pulled down in 1873, and only its grey tower was left standing beside Dartington Hall. The yews around it stayed. A reader sent us one of them, a few metres from the tower. It is a European yew, ancient by their word, its trunk about eight metres round by their own measure.

The Ancient Yew Group, which records old yews across Britain, lists three here. The biggest, a female tree west of the tower, has been measured since 1787, and in 2012 its trunk was 655 centimetres round near the ground. One recorder called it one of the most knobbly yew boles to be seen, and nails are still embedded in the wood. A fluted yew grows south-west of the tower and a sprawling one on a bank to the north. The group puts the biggest in its ancient band, trees of five to seven metres round.

The reader's photographs reached us later the same day. They show a squat bole of burrs and folds inside a rope ring among the gravestones, which fits the group's knobbly yew west of the tower. If we have picked the wrong one of the three, tell us.

Walk all the way round the tower before you leave.

trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-18 reader judge: sent by a reader through the app (submission 1177, sighting 2d01c8dc-05b6-421a-b6aa-6e113740a1cf), GPS fix 'standing at the tree' at 50.45166, -3.69483, species Taxus baccata, age 'Ancient', girth 800 cm, no note; the photograph never reached us (the sighting row has none). The fix is about 10 m from the listed tower of the former St Mary's (SX 79780 62693), round which the Ancient Yew Group lists three yews (401, 402, 6746; its map point is the site, not each trunk). Which trunk the reader stood at is not known: the story names the group's figures as the group's and the reader's 800 cm as theirs, and asks. Published as a reader's tree with a GPS fix and a written source (CLAUDE.md 'Verify', closed list). 2026-11-18 later: the two photographs arrived (sighting 2d01c8dc-05b6-421a-b6aa-6e113740a1cf and its -extra-1) and were viewed: the whole yew beside the stone tower, its huge burred and folded bole inside a rope ring, gravestones around it, crown of long limbs, daylight, colour. / the bole close up from the front, great burrs and swellings, rope ring and gravestones behind, daylight, colour, some lens flare. The burred bole on flat ground fits tree 401's description; the story says so and asks to be corrected.
